038/**
039 * Manages the lifecycles of {@link Coroutine}-based {@link Command Commands}. Commands may be
040 * scheduled directly using {@link #schedule(Command)}, or be bound to {@link Trigger Triggers} to
041 * automatically handle scheduling and cancellation based on internal or external events. User code
042 * is responsible for calling {@link #run()} periodically to update trigger conditions and execute
043 * scheduled commands. Most often, this is done by overriding {@link TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()} to
044 * include a call to {@code Scheduler.getDefault().run()}:
045 *
046 * <pre>{@code
047 * public class Robot extends TimedRobot {
048 *   @Override
049 *   public void robotPeriodic() {
050 *     // Update the scheduler on every loop
051 *     Scheduler.getDefault().run();
052 *   }
053 * }
054 * }</pre>
055 *
056 * <h2>Danger</h2>
057 *
058 * <p>The scheduler <i>must</i> be used in a single-threaded program. Commands must be scheduled and
059 * canceled by the same thread that runs the scheduler, and cannot be run in a virtual thread.
060 *
061 * <p><strong>Using the commands framework in a multithreaded environment can cause crashes in the
062 * Java virtual machine at any time, including on an official field during a match.</strong> The
063 * Java JIT compilers make assumptions that rely on coroutines being used on a single thread.
064 * Breaking those assumptions can cause incorrect JIT code to be generated with undefined behavior,
065 * potentially causing control issues or crashes deep in JIT-generated native code.
066 *
067 * <p><strong>Normal concurrency constructs like locks, atomic references, and synchronized blocks
068 * or methods cannot save you.</strong>
069 *
070 * <h2>Lifecycle</h2>
071 *
072 * <p>The {@link #run()} method runs six steps:
073 *
074 * <ol>
075 *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been scheduled
076 *       in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
077 *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
078 *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
079 *   <li>Call {@link #sideload(Consumer) periodic sideload functions}.
080 *   <li>Poll all registered triggers to queue and cancel commands.
081 *   <li>Queue default commands for any mechanisms without a running command. The queued commands
082 *       can be superseded by any manual scheduling or commands scheduled by triggers in the next
083 *       run.
084 *   <li>Start all queued commands. This happens after all triggers are checked in case multiple
085 *       commands with conflicting requirements are queued in the same update; the last command to
086 *       be queued takes precedence over the rest.
087 *   <li>Loop over all running commands, mounting and calling each in turn until they either exit or
088 *       call {@link Coroutine#yield()}. Commands run in the order in which they were scheduled.
089 * </ol>
090 *
091 * <h2>Telemetry</h2>
092 *
093 * <p>There are two mechanisms for telemetry for a scheduler. A protobuf serializer can be used to
094 * take a snapshot of a scheduler instance, and report what commands are queued (scheduled but have
095 * not yet started to run), commands that are running (along with timing data for each command), and
096 * total time spent in the most recent {@link #run()} call. However, it cannot detect one-shot
097 * commands that are scheduled, run, and complete all in a single {@code run()} invocation -
098 * effectively, commands that never call {@link Coroutine#yield()} are invisible.
099 *
100 * <p>A second telemetry mechanism is provided by {@link #addEventListener(Consumer)}. The scheduler
101 * will issue events to all registered listeners when certain events occur (see {@link
102 * SchedulerEvent} for all event types). These events are emitted immediately and can be used to
103 * detect lifecycle events for all commands, including one-shots that would be invisible to the
104 * protobuf serializer. However, it is up to the user to log those events themselves.
105 */
106public final class Scheduler implements ProtobufSerializable {
107  /**
108   * The default command bindings for each mechanism. Binding lists are ordered by priority; the
109   * last element in the list is the highest priority default command to be used. Bindings need to
110   * be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
111   */
112  private final Map<Mechanism, List<Binding>> m_defaultCommandBindings = new LinkedHashMap<>();
113
114  /**
115   * All bindings attached to this scheduler. This lets us cancel commands tied to scopes that go
116   * inactive. Bindings need to be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
117   */
118  private final Collection<Binding> m_activeBindings = new ArrayList<>();
119
120  /** Triggers with active command bindings that must not be allowed to be garbage collected. */
121  private final Set<Trigger> m_boundTriggers = new HashSet<>();
122
123  /** The set of commands scheduled since the start of the previous run. */
124  private final SequencedSet<CommandState> m_queuedToRun = new LinkedHashSet<>();
125
126  /**
127   * The states of all running commands (does not include on deck commands). We preserve insertion
128   * order to guarantee that child commands run after their parents.
129   */
130  private final SequencedMap<Command, CommandState> m_runningCommands = new LinkedHashMap<>();
131
132  /**
133   * The stack of currently executing commands. Child commands are pushed onto the stack and popped
134   * when they complete. Use {@link #currentState()} and {@link #currentCommand()} to get the
135   * currently executing command or its state.
136   */
137  private final Stack<CommandState> m_currentCommandAncestry = new Stack<>();
138
139  /** The periodic callbacks to run, outside of the command structure. */
140  private final List<PeriodicCallback> m_periodicCallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
141
142  /** Event loop for trigger bindings. */
143  private final EventLoop m_eventLoop = new EventLoop();
144
145  /** The scope for continuations to yield to. */
146  private final ContinuationScope m_scope = new ContinuationScope("coroutine commands");
147
148  /** Represents a single periodic callback. Stores a coroutine and its scope. */
149  private record PeriodicCallback(BindingScope scope, Coroutine coroutine) {}

189  /** Private constructor. Use static factory methods or the default scheduler instance. */
190  private Scheduler() {}

192  /**
193   * Sets the default command for a mechanism. The command must require that mechanism and cannot
194   * require any other mechanisms. If another default command has already been set for this
195   * mechanism, the one provided will supersede it.
196   *
197   * <p>If this is called inside a running opmode or in a running command, the default command
198   * setting will only apply while that opmode or command is active. When the opmode or command
199   * exits, the previous default command setting will be restored.
200   *
201   * <p>Commands running as default commands may call this method to change their mechanism's
202   * default command on the fly. The new default command will take effect at the end of the
203   * scheduler's loop cycle.
204   *
205   * @param mechanism the mechanism for which to set the default command
206   * @param defaultCommand the default command to execute on the mechanism
207   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the command does not meet the requirements for being a
208   *     default command
209   */
210  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
211  public void setDefaultCommand(Mechanism mechanism, Command defaultCommand) {
212    if (!defaultCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
213      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
214          "A mechanism's default command must require that mechanism");
215    }
216
217    if (defaultCommand.requirements().size() > 1) {
218      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
219          "A mechanism's default command cannot require other mechanisms");
220    }
221
222    var currentCommand = currentCommand();
223    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
224
225    var binding =
226        new Binding(
227            scope, BindingType.CONTINUOUSLY_SCHEDULE_WHILE_HIGH, defaultCommand, new Throwable());
228
229    var currentDefaultCommand = getDefaultCommandFor(mechanism);
230    m_defaultCommandBindings.computeIfAbsent(mechanism, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(binding);
231
232    if (currentCommand != null && currentCommand != currentDefaultCommand) {
233      // User called `setDefaultCommand` inside another command.
234      // Immediately reprocess the default commands for this mechanism to ensure it's in sync with
235      // the rest of the commands in the scheduler. This is required because we normally schedule
236      // the default commands at the start of the scheduler `run()` method, so the new default
237      // command wouldn't be handled until the next run (ie, the previous default command would
238      // still be active for the current iteration)
239      //
240      // Note that we cannot do this if the current default command is the caller because commands
241      // cannot be canceled while mounted.
242      processDefaultCommands(mechanism);
243    }
244  }
245
246  /**
247   * Gets the default command currently used for a mechanism.
248   *
249   * @param mechanism The mechanism
250   * @return The default command, or null if no default command was ever set
251   */
252  public Command getDefaultCommandFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
253    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
254    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
255      return null;
256    }
257
258    return bindings.getLast().command();
259  }
260
261  // package-private helper for unit test access
262  List<Binding> getDefaultCommandBindingsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
263    return m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
264  }

266  /**
267   * Adds a callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or control
268   * any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or LED
269   * data buffers), or perform some other helpful task. The callback is responsible for managing its
270   * own control flow and end conditions. If you want to run a single task periodically for the
271   * entire lifespan of the scheduler, use {@link #addPeriodic(Runnable)}.
272   *
273   * <p><strong>Note:</strong> Like commands, any loops in the callback must appropriately yield
274   * control back to the scheduler with {@link Coroutine#yield} or risk stalling your program in an
275   * unrecoverable infinite loop!
276   *
277   * <p>The coroutines provided to sideloaded functions will not cancel themselves if a fork or
278   * await call fails. This allows user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. You can opt
279   * into canceling the coroutine if a fork or await call fails by calling {@link
280   * Coroutine#setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)}.
281   *
282   * @param callback the callback to sideload
283   * @see #addPeriodic(Runnable)
284   */
285  public void sideload(Consumer<Coroutine> callback) {
286    var coroutine = new Coroutine(this, m_scope, callback);
287    // Sideloaded functions shouldn't be canceled if a command can't be forked. The default behavior
288    // should allow user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. This differs from
289    // coroutines issued to commands, which should fail by default to prevent unexpected robot state
290    coroutine.setCancelOnForkFailure(false);
291
292    var scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
293    m_periodicCallbacks.add(new PeriodicCallback(scope, coroutine));
294  }
295
296  /**
297   * Adds a periodic callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or
298   * control any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or
299   * LED data buffers), or perform some other helpful task.
300   *
301   * <p>For example:
302   *
303   * <pre>{@code
304   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
305   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> {
306   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("X", getX());
307   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("Y", getY());
308   * });
309   * }</pre>
310   *
311   * <p>{@code addPeriodic} is a convenience method that is identical to using {@link
312   * #sideload(Consumer)} with an unending {@code while} loop:
313   *
314   * <pre>{@code
315   * // An addPeriodic call:
316   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
317   *
318   * // Is equivalent to this sideload call:
319   * scheduler.sideload(coroutine -> {
320   *   while (true) {
321   *     leds.setData(ledDataBuffer)
322   *     coroutine.yield();
323   *   }
324   * });
325   * }</pre>
326   *
327   * @param callback the periodic function to run
328   * @see #sideload(Consumer)
329   */
330  public void addPeriodic(Runnable callback) {
331    sideload(
332        coroutine -> {
333          while (true) {
334            callback.run();
335            coroutine.yield();
336          }
337        });
338  }
339
340  /**
341   * Represents possible results of a command scheduling attempt. These can be used either as
342   * concrete results after a command was attempted to be scheduled, or as predictive results when
343   * checking if a command can be scheduled before committing to it.
344   */
345  public sealed interface ScheduleResult {
346    /**
347     * The command that was attempted to be scheduled.
348     *
349     * @return the command that was attempted to be scheduled
350     */
351    Command command();
352
353    /**
354     * Whether the scheduling attempt was successful.
355     *
356     * @return true if the scheduling attempt was successful, false if it failed
357     */
358    boolean successful();
359
360    /** Common interface for successful scheduling attempts. */
361    sealed interface Successful extends ScheduleResult {
362      @Override
363      default boolean successful() {
364        return true;
365      }
366    }
367
368    /** Common interface for failed scheduling attempts. */
369    sealed interface Failure extends ScheduleResult {
370      @Override
371      default boolean successful() {
372        return false;
373      }
374    }
375
376    /**
377     * A successful scheduling attempt.
378     *
379     * @param command the command that was successfully scheduled
380     */
381    record Success(Command command) implements Successful {
382      /**
383       * A successful scheduling attempt is always successful.
384       *
385       * @return true
386       */
387      @Override
388      public boolean successful() {
389        return true;
390      }
391    }
392
393    /**
394     * A scheduling attempt that was redundant because the command was already running.
395     *
396     * @param command the command that was attempted to be scheduled
397     */
398    record AlreadyRunning(Command command) implements Successful {
399      /**
400       * A scheduling attempt that was redundant because the command was already running is always
401       * successful.
402       *
403       * @return true
404       */
405      @Override
406      public boolean successful() {
407        return true;
408      }
409    }
410
411    /**
412     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a running
413     * command with shared requirements.
414     *
415     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
416     * @param alreadyRunning the running command that prevented the command from being scheduled
417     */
418    record LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(Command command, Command alreadyRunning)
419        implements Failure {}
420
421    /**
422     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a queued command
423     * with shared requirements.
424     *
425     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
426     * @param queuedCommand the queued command that prevented the command from being scheduled
427     */
428    record LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(Command command, Command queuedCommand)
429        implements Failure {}
430
431    /**
432     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the robot is in a disabled state and it requires one
433     * or more mechanisms that are not {@link Mechanism#controllableDuringDisabled() controllable
434     * during disabled}.
435     *
436     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
437     * @param unsafeMechanisms the uncontrollable mechanisms
438     */
439    record RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(Command command, Collection<Mechanism> unsafeMechanisms)
440        implements Failure {}
441  }
442
443  /**
444   * Checks if a command is able to be scheduled. Returns of the following states:
445   *
446   * <ul>
447   *   <li>{@link AlreadyRunning} if the command is already scheduled or running.
448   *   <li>{@link Success} if the command is not already scheduled or running and does not conflict
449   *       with any other scheduled or running commands.
450   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a
451   *       running command that shares requirements
452   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a queued
453   *       command that shares requirements
454   *   <li>{@link RequiresUnsafeMechanisms} if the command requires mechanisms that are not
455   *       controllable when the robot is disabled.
456   * </ul>
457   *
458   * @param command The command to check. Cannot be null.
459   * @return A schedule result indicating the schedulability of the command.
460   */
461  @NoDiscard
462  public ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Command command) {
463    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(command, "command", "isSchedulable");
464
465    if (isScheduledOrRunning(command)) {
466      return new AlreadyRunning(command);
467    }
468
469    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
470      var uncontrollables =
471          command.requirements().stream()
472              .filter(mechanism -> !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled())
473              .collect(Collectors.toSet());
474
475      if (!uncontrollables.isEmpty()) {
476        return new RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(command, uncontrollables);
477      }
478    }
479
480    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
481    for (var state = currentState(); state != null; state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
482      ancestry.add(state.command());
483    }
484
485    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
486  }
487
488  // similar to isSchedulable(Command), but used internally for processing bindings
489  // that may have command scopes.
490  private ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Binding binding) {
491    var command = binding.command();
492
493    if (isScheduledOrRunning(command)) {
494      return new AlreadyRunning(command);
495    }
496
497    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
498      var uncontrollables =
499          command.requirements().stream()
500              .filter(mechanism -> !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled())
501              .collect(Collectors.toSet());
502
503      if (!uncontrollables.isEmpty()) {
504        return new RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(command, uncontrollables);
505      }
506    }
507
508    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
509    if (binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand(Scheduler _, Command parent)) {
510      for (var state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
511          state != null;
512          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
513        ancestry.add(state.command());
514      }
515    } else {
516      for (var state = currentState();
517          state != null;
518          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
519        ancestry.add(state.command());
520      }
521    }
522
523    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
524  }
525
526  private Scheduler.ScheduleResult isSchedulableFromPriority(
527      Command command, Set<Command> ancestry) {
528    var running = m_runningCommands.values();
529    Command conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, running);
530    if (conflict != null) {
531      return new LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(command, conflict);
532    }
533
534    conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, m_queuedToRun);
535    if (conflict != null) {
536      return new LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(command, conflict);
537    }
538
539    return new Success(command);
540  }
541
542  /**
543   * Schedules a command to run. If one command schedules another (a "parent" and "child"), the
544   * child command will be canceled when the parent command completes. It is not possible to fork a
545   * child command and have it live longer than its parent.
546   *
547   * <p>Does nothing if the command is already scheduled or running, or requires at least one
548   * mechanism already used by a higher priority command.
549   *
550   * <p>For purposes of scheduling, a child command is considered to have a priority equal to the
551   * highest priority in its scheduling hierarchy. For example, if a parent command with priority 10
552   * schedules a child command with priority 5, the child command will be treated as having a
553   * priority of 10 and will interrupt any conflicting command with a priority of 10 or lower,
554   * rather than the usual 5.
555   *
556   * @param command the command to schedule
557   * @return the result of the scheduling attempt. See {@link ScheduleResult} for details.
558   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if scheduled by a command composition that has already
559   *     scheduled another command that shares at least one required mechanism
560   */
561  // Implementation detail: a child command will immediately start running when scheduled by a
562  // parent command, skipping the queue entirely. This avoids dead loop cycles where a parent
563  // schedules a child, appending it to the queue, then waits for the next cycle to pick it up and
564  // start it. With deeply nested commands, dead loops could quickly to add up and cause the
565  // innermost commands that actually _do_ something to start running hundreds of milliseconds after
566  // their root ancestor was scheduled.
567  public ScheduleResult schedule(Command command) {
568    // Get the narrowest binding scope.
569    // This prevents commands from outliving the opmodes that scheduled them, or from outliving
570    // their parents (eg if someone writes a command that manually calls schedule(Command) instead
571    // of using triggers to do so).
572    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
573
574    // Note: we use a throwable here instead of Thread.currentThread().getStackTrace() for easier
575    //       stack frame filtering and modification.
576    var binding = new Binding(scope, BindingType.IMMEDIATE, command, new Throwable());
577
578    return schedule(binding);
579  }
580
581  // Package-private for use by Trigger
582  ScheduleResult schedule(Binding binding) {
583    var command = binding.command();
584
585    var result = isSchedulable(binding);
586    if (!(result instanceof Success)) {
587      // We check specifically for Success, instead of `successful()`, because only a Success
588      // indicates that the command can actually go through the scheduling process. AlreadyRunning
589      // means what it says on the tin, and it would be incorrect to run the command back through
590      // the scheduling process.
591      return result;
592    }
593
594    if (!(binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand)) {
595      // Track this binding so we can disable it when it's out of scope.
596      // Note that, even though triggers can clean themselves up, commands that are manually
597      // scheduled cannot do the same, so we have to track them in the scheduler.
598
599      // We don't bother tracking command-scoped bindings; the bound command will already be
600      // cleaned up in the same cycle that the parent command exits, so this would attempt to
601      // double-cancel a child command across two cycles (once when the parent exits, and then in
602      // the next cycle in cancelStaleBindings). That would cause problems if the command object
603      // is immediately rescheduled as cancelStaleBindings would immediately cancel the new run
604      m_activeBindings.add(binding);
605    }
606
607    // Evict conflicting on-deck commands
608    // We check above if the input command is lower priority than any of these,
609    // so at this point we're guaranteed to be >= priority than anything already on deck
610    evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(command);
611
612    // If the binding is scoped to a particular command, that command is the parent. If we're in the
613    // middle of a run cycle and running commands, the parent is whatever command is currently
614    // running. Otherwise, there is no parent command.
615    var parentCommand =
616        binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand scope
617            ? scope.command()
618            : currentCommand();
619    var state = new CommandState(command, parentCommand, buildCoroutine(command), binding);
620
621    emitScheduledEvent(command);
622
623    if (currentState() != null) {
624      // Scheduling a child command while running. Start it immediately instead of waiting a full
625      // cycle. This prevents issues with deeply nested command groups taking many scheduler cycles
626      // to start running the commands that actually _do_ things
627      evictConflictingRunningCommands(state);
628      m_runningCommands.put(command, state);
629      runCommand(state);
630    } else {
631      // Scheduling outside a command, add it to the pending set. If it's not overridden by another
632      // conflicting command being scheduled in the same scheduler loop, it'll be promoted and
633      // start to run when #runCommands() is called
634      m_queuedToRun.add(state);
635    }
636
637    return result;
638  }
639
640  /**
641   * Checks if a command conflicts with and is a lower priority than any running command. Used when
642   * determining if the command can be scheduled.
643   *
644   * @return The conflicting command, or null if there is no conflict
645   */
646  private Command lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(
647      Command command, Collection<Command> ancestry, Collection<CommandState> checkAgainst) {
648    int maxAncestorPriority = command.priority();
649    for (Command ancestor : ancestry) {
650      maxAncestorPriority = Math.max(maxAncestorPriority, ancestor.priority());
651    }
652
653    // Check for conflicts with the commands that are already running
654    for (var state : checkAgainst) {
655      if (ancestry.contains(state.command())) {
656        // Can't conflict with an ancestor command
657        continue;
658      }
659
660      var c = state.command();
661      if (c.conflictsWith(command) && maxAncestorPriority < effectivePriority(state)) {
662        return c;
663      }
664    }
665
666    return null;
667  }
668
669  /**
670   * Calculates the effective priority of a command, taking into account the priorities of its
671   * ancestors.
672   *
673   * @param state The command state to check
674   * @return The effective priority of the command
675   */
676  private int effectivePriority(CommandState state) {
677    int max = state.command().priority();
678    for (var parent = state.parent(); parent != null; parent = state.parent()) {
679      state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
680      max = Math.max(max, parent.priority());
681    }
682    return max;
683  }
684
685  private void evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(Command command) {
686    for (var iterator = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
687      var scheduledState = iterator.next();
688      var scheduledCommand = scheduledState.command();
689      if (scheduledCommand.conflictsWith(command)) {
690        // Remove the lower priority conflicting command from the on deck commands.
691        // We don't need to call removeOrphanedChildren here because it hasn't started yet,
692        // meaning it hasn't had a chance to schedule any children
693        iterator.remove();
694        emitInterruptedEvent(scheduledCommand, command);
695        emitCanceledEvent(scheduledCommand);
696      }
697    }
698  }
699
700  /**
701   * Cancels all running commands with which an incoming state conflicts. Ancestor commands of the
702   * incoming state will not be canceled.
703   */
704  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
705  private void evictConflictingRunningCommands(CommandState incomingState) {
706    // The set of root states with which the incoming state conflicts but does not inherit from
707    Set<CommandState> conflictingRootStates =
708        m_runningCommands.values().stream()
709            .filter(state -> incomingState.command().conflictsWith(state.command()))
710            .filter(state -> !isAncestorOf(state.command(), incomingState))
711            .map(
712                state -> {
713                  // Find the highest level ancestor of the conflicting command from which the
714                  // incoming state does _not_ inherit. If they're totally unrelated, this will
715                  // get the very root ancestor; otherwise, it'll return a direct sibling of the
716                  // incoming command
717                  CommandState root = state;
718                  while (root.parent() != null && root.parent() != incomingState.parent()) {
719                    root = m_runningCommands.get(root.parent());
720                  }
721                  return root;
722                })
723            .collect(Collectors.toSet());
724
725    // Cancel the root commands
726    for (var conflictingState : conflictingRootStates) {
727      emitInterruptedEvent(conflictingState.command(), incomingState.command());
728      cancel(conflictingState.command());
729    }
730  }
731
732  /**
733   * Checks if a particular command is an ancestor of another.
734   *
735   * @param ancestor the potential ancestor for which to search
736   * @param state the state to check
737   * @return true if {@code ancestor} is the direct parent or indirect ancestor, false if not
738   */
739  @SuppressWarnings({"PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals", "PMD.SimplifyBooleanReturns"})
740  private boolean isAncestorOf(Command ancestor, CommandState state) {
741    if (state.parent() == null) {
742      // No parent, cannot inherit
743      return false;
744    }
745    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(ancestor)) {
746      // The given ancestor isn't running
747      return false;
748    }
749    if (state.parent() == ancestor) {
750      // Direct child
751      return true;
752    }
753    // Check if the command's parent inherits from the given ancestor
754    return m_runningCommands.values().stream()
755        .filter(s -> state.parent() == s.command())
756        .anyMatch(s -> isAncestorOf(ancestor, s));
757  }
758
759  /**
760   * Cancels a command and any other command scheduled by it. This occurs immediately and does not
761   * need to wait for a call to {@link #run()}. Any command that it scheduled will also be canceled
762   * to ensure commands within compositions do not continue to run.
763   *
764   * <p>This has no effect if the given command is not currently scheduled or running.
765   *
766   * @param command the command to cancel
767   */
768  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
769  public void cancel(Command command) {
770    var currentState = currentState();
771    if (currentState != null && command == currentState.command()) {
772      currentState.coroutine().requestCancellation(); // yields internally
773      return;
774    }
775
776    boolean running = isRunning(command);
777
778    // Evict the command. The next call to run() will schedule the default command for all its
779    // required mechanisms, unless another command requiring those mechanisms is scheduled between
780    // calling cancel() and calling run()
781    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
782    boolean queued = m_queuedToRun.removeIf(state -> state.command() == command);
783
784    if (running) {
785      // Only run the hooks if the command was running. If it was on deck or not
786      // even in the scheduler at the time, then there's nothing to do
787      // Always run onExit first, in case cancellation has special behavior that overrides
788      // standard exit logic.
789      command.onExit();
790      command.onCancel();
791    }
792
793    if (running || queued) {
794      // Emit a cancellation event only if the given command was in the scheduler
795      emitCanceledEvent(command);
796    }
797
798    // Clean up any orphaned child commands; their lifespan must not exceed the parent's
799    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
800  }
801
802  /**
803   * Updates the command scheduler. This will run operations in the following order:
804   *
805   * <ol>
806   *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been
807   *       scheduled in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
808   *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
809   *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
810   *   <li>Run sideloaded functions from {@link #sideload(Consumer)} and {@link
811   *       #addPeriodic(Runnable)}
812   *   <li>Update trigger bindings to queue and cancel bound commands
813   *   <li>Queue default commands for mechanisms that do not have a queued or running command
814   *   <li>Promote queued commands to the running set
815   *   <li>For every command in the running set, mount and run that command until it calls {@link
816   *       Coroutine#yield()} or exits
817   * </ol>
818   *
819   * <p>This method is intended to be called in a periodic loop like {@link
820   * TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()}
821   */
822  public void run() {
823    final long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
824
825    // Cancel any commands with stale binding scopes
826    cancelStaleBindings();
827
828    // Unbind any triggers with stale creation scopes.
829    // This allows triggers that can never be used again to be garbage collected to reduce
830    // memory usage and avoid potential OOMs from poorly written user code.
831    unbindStaleTriggers();
832
833    // If the robot is disabled, cancel any commands that require uncontrollable mechanisms
834    cancelCommandsThatCannotRunInDisabled();
835
836    // Sideloads may change some state that affects triggers. Run them first.
837    runPeriodicSideloads();
838
839    // Poll triggers next to schedule and cancel commands
840    m_eventLoop.poll();
841
842    // Schedule default commands for any mechanisms that don't have a running command and didn't
843    // have a new command scheduled by a sideload function or a trigger
844    scheduleDefaultCommands();
845
846    // Move all scheduled commands to the running set
847    promoteScheduledCommands();
848
849    // Run every command in order until they call Coroutine.yield() or exit
850    runCommands();
851
852    final long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
853    m_lastRunTimeMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
854  }
855
856  private void cancelStaleBindings() {
857    for (var iterator = m_activeBindings.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
858      var binding = iterator.next();
859      if (binding.scope().active()) {
860        continue;
861      }
862      cancel(binding.command());
863      iterator.remove();
864    }
865  }
866
867  private void unbindStaleTriggers() {
868    // Remove strong references to any triggers that have gone stale. This allows triggers to be
869    // garbage collected if they're not referenced outside the scope that created them. We don't
870    // clear any command bindings or unbind it from the event loop; otherwise, cached triggers
871    // would stop being updated until new command bindings are added.
872    for (var iterator = m_boundTriggers.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
873      var trigger = iterator.next();
874      if (!trigger.isScopeActive()) {
875        iterator.remove();
876      }
877    }
878  }
879
880  private void cancelCommandsThatCannotRunInDisabled() {
881    if (RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
882      // Nothing to do if the robot is enabled
883      return;
884    }
885
886    List<Command> commandsToCancel = new ArrayList<>();
887
888    for (var runningState : m_runningCommands.values()) {
889      var command = runningState.command();
890      boolean canRun = true;
891      for (var mechanism : command.requirements()) {
892        if (!mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
893          canRun = false;
894          break;
895        }
896      }
897
898      if (canRun) {
899        continue;
900      }
901
902      commandsToCancel.add(getRoot(command));
903    }
904
905    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
906      var command = queuedState.command();
907
908      boolean canRun = true;
909      for (var mechanism : command.requirements()) {
910        if (!mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
911          canRun = false;
912          break;
913        }
914      }
915
916      if (canRun) {
917        continue;
918      }
919
920      commandsToCancel.add(command);
921    }
922
923    for (var command : commandsToCancel) {
924      cancel(command);
925    }
926  }
927
928  /**
929   * Adds a bound trigger to this scheduler. The trigger will be unbound from the event loop when
930   * its creation scope becomes inactive and may be eligible for garbage collection.
931   */
932  // package-private for Trigger
933  void addBoundTrigger(Trigger trigger) {
934    m_boundTriggers.add(trigger);
935  }
936
937  /**
938   * Removes strong retention for a trigger, allowing it to potentially be garbage collected if no
939   * other references to it remain.
940   */
941  // package-private for Trigger
942  void removeBoundTrigger(Trigger trigger) {
943    m_boundTriggers.remove(trigger);
944  }
945
946  private void promoteScheduledCommands() {
947    // Clear any commands that conflict with the scheduled set
948    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
949      evictConflictingRunningCommands(queuedState);
950    }
951
952    // Move any scheduled commands to the running set
953    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
954      m_runningCommands.put(queuedState.command(), queuedState);
955    }
956
957    // Clear the set of on-deck commands,
958    // since we just put them all into the set of running commands
959    m_queuedToRun.clear();
960  }
961
962  private void runPeriodicSideloads() {
963    for (var iterator = m_periodicCallbacks.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
964      PeriodicCallback callback = iterator.next();
965      if (!callback.scope().active()) {
966        // The callback's enclosing scope exited - remove without running it and move on
967        iterator.remove();
968        continue;
969      }
970
971      // Update periodic callbacks
972      Coroutine coroutine = callback.coroutine();
973      coroutine.mount();
974      try {
975        coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
976      } finally {
977        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
978      }
979
980      if (coroutine.isDone()
981          || coroutine.isInterruptRequested()
982          || coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
983        // Callback finished or requested early termination - remove it from the list
984        iterator.remove();
985      }
986    }
987  }
988
989  private void runCommands() {
990    // TODO: Track command roots and run the commands in each root in reverse order, but run the
991    //       roots in insertion order
992    // Tick every command that hasn't been completed yet
993    // Run in reverse so parent commands can resume in the same loop cycle an awaited child command
994    // completes. Otherwise, parents could only resume on the next loop cycle, introducing a delay
995    // at every layer of nesting.
996    for (var state : List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.values()).reversed()) {
997      runCommand(state);
998    }
999  }
1000
1001  /**
1002   * Mounts and runs a command until it yields or exits.
1003   *
1004   * @param state The command state to run
1005   */
1006  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidCatchingGenericException")
1007  private void runCommand(CommandState state) {
1008    final var command = state.command();
1009    final var coroutine = state.coroutine();
1010
1011    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1012      // Probably canceled by an owning composition, do not run
1013      return;
1014    }
1015
1016    var previousState = currentState();
1017
1018    m_currentCommandAncestry.push(state);
1019    long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
1020    emitMountedEvent(command);
1021    coroutine.mount();
1022    try {
1023      coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
1024    } catch (RuntimeException e) {
1025      // Command encountered an uncaught exception.
1026      handleCommandException(state, e);
1027    } finally {
1028      long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
1029      double elapsedMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
1030      state.setLastRuntimeMs(elapsedMs);
1031
1032      if (state.equals(currentState())) {
1033        // Remove the command we just ran from the top of the stack
1034        m_currentCommandAncestry.pop();
1035      }
1036
1037      if (previousState != null) {
1038        // Remount the parent command, if there is one
1039        previousState.coroutine().mount();
1040      } else {
1041        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
1042      }
1043    }
1044
1045    if (coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
1046      cancel(command);
1047    } else if (coroutine.isDone()) {
1048      handleCommandCompletion(command);
1049    } else if (coroutine.isInterruptRequested()) {
1050      handleCoroutineIRQ(coroutine, command);
1051    } else {
1052      // Yielded
1053      emitYieldedEvent(command);
1054    }
1055  }
1056
1057  private void handleCommandCompletion(Command command) {
1058    command.onExit();
1059    emitCompletedEvent(command);
1060    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
1061    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
1062  }
1063
1064  private void handleCoroutineIRQ(Coroutine coroutine, Command command) {
1065    Command root = getRoot(command); // capture the root command before modifying scheduler state
1066    m_currentCommandAncestry.clear();
1067    emitForkFailureEvent(command, coroutine.getForkResult().getFailedCommands());
1068    cancel(root);
1069    Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
1070  }
1071
1072  /**
1073   * Handles uncaught runtime exceptions from a mounted and running command. The command's ancestor
1074   * and child commands will all be canceled and the exception's backtrace will be modified to
1075   * include the stack frames of the schedule call site.
1076   *
1077   * @param state The state of the command that encountered the exception.
1078   * @param e The exception that was thrown.
1079   * @throws RuntimeException rethrows the exception, with a modified backtrace pointing to the
1080   *     schedule site
1081   */
1082  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1083  private void handleCommandException(CommandState state, RuntimeException e) {
1084    var command = state.command();
1085
1086    // Fetch the root command
1087    // (needs to be done before removing the failed command from the running set)
1088    final Command root = getRoot(command);
1089
1090    // Remove it from the running set.
1091    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
1092
1093    // Intercept the exception, inject stack frames from the schedule site, and rethrow it
1094    var binding = state.binding();
1095    e.setStackTrace(
1096        CommandTraceHelper.modifyTrace(
1097            e.getStackTrace(), binding.stackTraceStore().getStackTrace()));
1098    emitCompletedWithErrorEvent(command, e);
1099
1100    // Clean up child commands after emitting the event so child Canceled events are emitted
1101    // after the parent's CompletedWithError
1102    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
1103
1104    // Bubble up to the root and cancel all commands between the root and this one
1105    // Note: Because we remove the command from the running set above, we still need to
1106    //       clean up all the failed command's children
1107    if (root != null && root != command) {
1108      cancel(root);
1109    }
1110
1111    // Then rethrow the exception
1112    throw e;
1113  }
1114
1115  /**
1116   * Gets the currently executing command state, or null if no command is currently executing.
1117   *
1118   * @return the currently executing command state
1119   */
1120  private CommandState currentState() {
1121    if (m_currentCommandAncestry.isEmpty()) {
1122      // Avoid EmptyStackException
1123      return null;
1124    }
1125
1126    return m_currentCommandAncestry.peek();
1127  }
1128
1129  /**
1130   * Gets the currently executing command, or null if no command is currently executing.
1131   *
1132   * @return the currently executing command
1133   */
1134  public Command currentCommand() {
1135    var state = currentState();
1136    if (state == null) {
1137      return null;
1138    }
1139
1140    return state.command();
1141  }
1142
1143  private void scheduleDefaultCommands() {
1144    m_defaultCommandBindings.keySet().forEach(this::processDefaultCommands);
1145  }
1146
1147  private void processDefaultCommands(Mechanism mechanism) {
1148    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.get(mechanism);
1149
1150    // Remove default command bindings that are no longer active.
1151    // If a default command is running when its scope goes inactive, also be sure to cancel it.
1152    bindings.removeIf(
1153        b -> {
1154          if (!b.scope().active()) {
1155            cancel(b.command());
1156            return true;
1157          }
1158          return false;
1159        });
1160
1161    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
1162      // Nothing to do. No active bindings remain.
1163      return;
1164    }
1165
1166    // Cancel any default command except the narrowest-scoped one (the last binding in the list)
1167    for (int i = 0; i < bindings.size() - 1; i++) {
1168      Command widerScopeDefaultCommand = bindings.get(i).command();
1169      cancel(widerScopeDefaultCommand);
1170    }
1171
1172    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled() && !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
1173      // Default commands can never be scheduled if the robot is disabled and the mechanism is not
1174      // controllable during disabled, so there's no point in attempting to queue the default
1175      // command
1176      return;
1177    }
1178
1179    // Check if the mechanism is currently in use. We can queue the default command if it's not.
1180    for (Command runningCommand : m_runningCommands.keySet()) {
1181      if (runningCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
1182        return;
1183      }
1184    }
1185    for (CommandState queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
1186      if (queuedState.command().requires(mechanism)) {
1187        return;
1188      }
1189    }
1190
1191    // Nothing currently running or queued that needs this mechanism. Queue the default command.
1192    var defaultCommand = bindings.getLast();
1193    schedule(defaultCommand);
1194  }
1195
1196  /**
1197   * Removes all commands descended from a parent command. This is used to ensure that any command
1198   * scheduled within a composition or group cannot live longer than any ancestor.
1199   *
1200   * @param parent the root command whose descendants to remove from the scheduler
1201   */
1202  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1203  private void removeOrphanedChildren(Command parent) {
1204    m_runningCommands.entrySet().stream()
1205        .filter(e -> e.getValue().parent() == parent)
1206        .toList() // copy to an intermediate list to avoid concurrent modification
1207        .forEach(e -> cancel(e.getKey()));
1208  }
1209
1210  /**
1211   * Builds a coroutine object that the command will be bound to. The coroutine will be scoped to
1212   * this scheduler object and cannot be used by another scheduler instance.
1213   *
1214   * @param command the command for which to build a coroutine
1215   * @return the binding coroutine
1216   */
1217  private Coroutine buildCoroutine(Command command) {
1218    return new Coroutine(this, m_scope, command::run);
1219  }
1220
1221  /**
1222   * Checks if a command is currently running.
1223   *
1224   * @param command the command to check
1225   * @return true if the command is running, false if not
1226   */
1227  public boolean isRunning(Command command) {
1228    return m_runningCommands.containsKey(command);
1229  }
1230
1231  /**
1232   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, but is not yet running.
1233   *
1234   * @param command the command to check
1235   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run, false if not
1236   */
1237  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1238  public boolean isScheduled(Command command) {
1239    return m_queuedToRun.stream().anyMatch(state -> state.command() == command);
1240  }
1241
1242  /**
1243   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, or is already running.
1244   *
1245   * @param command the command to check
1246   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run or is already running, false if not
1247   */
1248  public boolean isScheduledOrRunning(Command command) {
1249    return isScheduled(command) || isRunning(command);
1250  }
1251
1252  /**
1253   * Gets the set of all currently running commands. Commands are returned in the order in which
1254   * they were scheduled. The returned set is read-only.
1255   *
1256   * @return the currently running commands
1257   */
1258  public Collection<Command> getRunningCommands() {
1259    return List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.keySet());
1260  }
1261
1262  /**
1263   * Gets all the currently running commands that require a particular mechanism. Commands are
1264   * returned in the order in which they were scheduled. The returned list is read-only.
1265   *
1266   * @param mechanism the mechanism to get the commands for
1267   * @return the currently running commands that require the mechanism.
1268   */
1269  public List<Command> getRunningCommandsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
1270    return m_runningCommands.keySet().stream()
1271        .filter(command -> command.requires(mechanism))
1272        .toList();
1273  }
1274
1275  /**
1276   * Cancels all currently running and scheduled commands. All default commands will be scheduled on
1277   * the next call to {@link #run()}, unless a higher priority command is scheduled or triggered
1278   * after {@code cancelAll()} is used.
1279   */
1280  public void cancelAll() {
1281    for (var onDeckIter = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); onDeckIter.hasNext(); ) {
1282      var state = onDeckIter.next();
1283      onDeckIter.remove();
1284      emitCanceledEvent(state.command());
1285    }
1286
1287    for (var liveIter = m_runningCommands.entrySet().iterator(); liveIter.hasNext(); ) {
1288      var entry = liveIter.next();
1289      liveIter.remove();
1290      Command canceledCommand = entry.getKey();
1291      // Always run onExit first, in case cancellation has special behavior that overrides
1292      // standard exit logic.
1293      canceledCommand.onExit();
1294      canceledCommand.onCancel();
1295      emitCanceledEvent(canceledCommand);
1296    }
1297  }
1298
1299  /**
1300   * An event loop used by the scheduler to poll triggers that schedule or cancel commands. This
1301   * event loop is always polled on every call to {@link #run()}. Custom event loops need to be
1302   * bound to this one for synchronicity with the scheduler; however, they can always be polled
1303   * manually before or after the call to {@link #run()}.
1304   *
1305   * @return the default event loop.
1306   */
1307  @NoDiscard
1308  public EventLoop getDefaultEventLoop() {
1309    return m_eventLoop;
1310  }
1311
1312  /**
1313   * For internal use.
1314   *
1315   * @return The commands that have been scheduled but not yet started.
1316   */
1317  @NoDiscard
1318  public Collection<Command> getQueuedCommands() {
1319    return m_queuedToRun.stream().map(CommandState::command).toList();
1320  }
1321
1322  private Command getRoot(Command command) {
1323    Command root = command;
1324    Command parent = getParentOf(command);
1325    while (parent != null) {
1326      root = parent;
1327      parent = getParentOf(parent);
1328    }
1329
1330    return root;
1331  }
1332
1333  /**
1334   * For internal use.
1335   *
1336   * @param command The command to check
1337   * @return The command that forked the provided command. Null if the command is not a child of
1338   *     another command.
1339   */
1340  public Command getParentOf(Command command) {
1341    var state = m_runningCommands.get(command);
1342    if (state == null) {
1343      return null;
1344    }
1345    return state.parent();
1346  }
1347
1348  /**
1349   * Gets how long a command took to run in the previous cycle. If the command is not currently
1350   * running, returns -1.
1351   *
1352   * @param command The command to check
1353   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command last took to execute.
1354   */
1355  public double lastCommandRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1356    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1357      return m_runningCommands.get(command).lastRuntimeMs();
1358    } else {
1359      return -1;
1360    }
1361  }
1362
1363  /**
1364   * Gets how long a command has taken to run, in aggregate, since it was most recently scheduled.
1365   * If the command is not currently running, returns -1.
1366   *
1367   * @param command The command to check
1368   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command has taken to execute in total
1369   */
1370  public double totalRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1371    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1372      return m_runningCommands.get(command).totalRuntimeMs();
1373    } else {
1374      // Not running; no data
1375      return -1;
1376    }
1377  }
1378
1379  /**
1380   * Gets the unique run id for a scheduled or running command. If the command is not currently
1381   * scheduled or running, this function returns {@code 0}.
1382   *
1383   * @param command The command to get the run ID for
1384   * @return The run of the command
1385   */
1386  @NoDiscard
1387  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1388  public int runId(Command command) {
1389    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1390      return m_runningCommands.get(command).id();
1391    }
1392
1393    // Check scheduled commands
1394    for (var scheduled : m_queuedToRun) {
1395      if (scheduled.command() == command) {
1396        return scheduled.id();
1397      }
1398    }
1399
1400    return 0;
1401  }
1402
1403  /**
1404   * Gets how long the scheduler took to process its most recent {@link #run()} invocation, in
1405   * milliseconds. Defaults to -1 if the scheduler has not yet run.
1406   *
1407   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the scheduler last took to execute.
1408   */
1409  @NoDiscard
1410  public double lastRuntimeMs() {
1411    return m_lastRunTimeMs;
1412  }

1414  // Event-base telemetry and helpers. The static factories are for convenience to automatically
1415  // set the timestamp instead of littering RobotController.getTime() everywhere.
1416
1417  private void emitScheduledEvent(Command command) {
1418    var event = new SchedulerEvent.Scheduled(command, RobotController.getTime());
1419    emitEvent(event);
1420  }

1457  /**
1458   * Adds a listener to handle events that are emitted by the scheduler. Events are emitted when
1459   * certain actions are taken by user code or by internal processing logic in the scheduler.
1460   * Listeners should take care to be quick, simple, and not schedule or cancel commands, as that
1461   * may cause inconsistent scheduler behavior or even cause a program crash.
1462   *
1463   * <p>Listeners are primarily expected to be for data logging and telemetry. In particular, a
1464   * one-shot command (one that never calls {@link Coroutine#yield()}) will never appear in the
1465   * standard protobuf telemetry because it is scheduled, runs, and finishes all in a single
1466   * scheduler cycle. However, {@link SchedulerEvent.Scheduled},{@link SchedulerEvent.Mounted}, and
1467   * {@link SchedulerEvent.Completed} events will be emitted corresponding to those actions, and
1468   * user code can listen for and log such events.
1469   *
1470   * @param listener The listener to add. Cannot be null.
1471   * @throws NullPointerException if given a null listener
1472   */
1473  public void addEventListener(Consumer<? super SchedulerEvent> listener) {
1474    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(listener, "listener", "addEventListener");
1475
1476    m_eventListeners.add(listener);
1477  }
1478
1479  private void emitEvent(SchedulerEvent event) {
1480    // TODO: Prevent listeners from interacting with the scheduler.
1481    //       Scheduling or canceling commands while the scheduler is processing will probably cause
1482    //       bugs in user code or even a program crash.
1483    for (var listener : m_eventListeners) {
1484      listener.accept(event);
1485    }
1486  }
1487}
